newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends down on stk mkt fears.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends down on stk mkt fears.

text.p: * Central Bank seen selling dollars at 26.37 pesos
The Philippine peso was pulled down on Tuesday on fears of possible large outflows as a result of the stock market's tumble, traders said.
It ended at 26.37 from the previous close of 26.367.
The day's average was at 26.369 from 26.368, with volume higher at $150.9 million from $102.5 million.
"It was more of market positioning for possible outflows for tomorrow," a foreign bank dealer said.
"If the Central Bank stays firm at 26.37, then the peso will hold at that level," the trader said.
Traders said they saw the Central Bank sell $15 million to $22 million at 26.37 pesos in late trade on Tuesday.
"Those who were short on dollars decided to buy back," another trader said.

A dealer said the Central Bank's announcement on Tuesday that it will limit banks' exposure to the property sector to 20 percent of their total loan portfolio could help rally the stock market and prevent outflows.
